summary: We are introducing ingress policies in preview. An ingress policy admits or blocks a request by combining several conditions in one policy. This preview includes the following capabilities: Combined admission rules. Evaluate network origin, authentication method, client, geolocation, PrivateLink ID, and endpoint path in one policy. Combine the conditions with AND, OR, and NOT, then allow or block the request. For example, allow drivers from the corporate network and block a specific application, or allow single sign-on only from approved countries. Difference from network and authentication policies. A network policy controls network locations and private connectivity. An authentication policy controls authentication methods, clients, security integrations, and multi-factor authentication. An ingress policy makes one allow-or-block decision from several of these signals together, including geolocation and endpoint path. Snowflake evaluates each policy on its own. A request is admitted only when every applicable policy allows it. Login and subsequent requests. Snowflake evaluates the policy when a user logs in and again on every subsequent authenticated request through drivers and APIs, so a policy change can affect existing sessions.
title: Ingress policies (Preview)
